content: The Resident Survival Guide Project is a collaborative initiative involving WikiDoc editors, associate editors, and assistant editors who possess prior expertise in medical education and training across various specialties. This project is structured in a straightforward yet effective manner to address common medical conditions frequently encountered by medical graduates in training, such as interns, residents, and house staff officers. The primary aim of this project is to enhance the clinical skills of medical and surgical residents across different specialties, enabling them to accurately evaluate, diagnose, and treat patients presenting with acute medical problems. Additionally, the project emphasizes the implementation of evidence-based approaches that healthcare professionals should adhere to when managing common public health conditions. Statement of Need Interns and residents worldwide, despite differences in culture and circumstances, share several common needs. These include: A quick and efficient method to diagnose and treat acute medical problems without the need to consult lengthy monographs during emergency situations. A simple and accessible guide to stay updated on the latest approaches and standards of care for managing common acute medical emergencies. A systematic approach to emergency situations that helps minimize medical errors, which are often encountered by interns and residents due to extended work hours. How WikiDoc Can Meet These Needs A collaborative effort has been initiated among the WikiDoc leadership, on-campus scholars, and remote contributors to provide residents globally with a concise and efficient guide to managing acute medical conditions commonly faced by house staff. The WikiDoc Resident Survival Guide Project specifically targets house staff in its approach. This project aims to improve the ability of medical and surgical residents across various specialties to effectively evaluate, diagnose, and treat patients presenting with acute medical issues. It also incorporates evidence-based practices that healthcare professionals should follow when addressing common public health conditions. How You Can Help WikiDoc Meet These Needs The Resident Survival Guide Project values contributions from medical professionals with prior graduate training or clinical practice experience. These contributors may include: Medical and surgical residents and fellows. Attending physicians. Lecturers, instructors, associate professors, and full professors in medical schools within their respective fields of expertise. Postdoctoral fellows with prior or current medical practice experience. WikiDoc welcomes remote contributions from qualified individuals. If you are interested and qualified to participate in the Resident Survival Guide Project, the WikiDoc Foundation encourages you to reach out. They will provide guidance on how to get started. Once you join as an editor, you will have the opportunity to select your area of expertise and begin editing. This collaborative effort ensures that the Resident Survival Guide Project continues to grow and expand, addressing an increasing number of emergency medical conditions encountered by house officers worldwide.
